clue.text: Five hundred struggle in rush for equipment

indicators.note: the first words sit inside the word for 'rush', placed within it

blocks.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
a war is a struggle between forces
to hare is to run or rush along

explanation.surface: Someone hurriedly grabs gear amid a scrum of five hundred shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' reads as a hurry in the surface, but it is the verb to hare, run fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardware means tools, machinery and other physical kit, so it is a fair synonym for equipment.

clue.text: Scripture worthily translated

indicators.note: translating turns text into a new form, so the letters are rewritten in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sacred text has been rendered into another language with due care.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy writ is the sacred writing of a religion, especially the Bible, which is what scripture means.

clue.text: Change course of revolutionary anger with court

blocks.note: a Red is a communist revolutionary
ire is a literary word for anger
CT is the standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A furious rebel's rage, combined with legal action, alters the direction of events.
explanation.definitionFit: To redirect something is to send it along a different route, changing where it is heading.

clue.text: Range and depth in humour over hour

indicators.note: one word is put inside another, sitting within it
in a down clue, being over means coming above, so that piece is written first

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for depth
wit is clever humour
H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A comedian's material is praised for its breadth and profundity, timed over an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' means the first part sits above the hour's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Width is the extent or breadth of something, as in the range of a person's interests.

clue.text: Resounding conclusion of censor, constantly criticising

indicators.note: a conclusion is an end, so only the final letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the last letter of censor
ever means always or constantly
berating is scolding or criticising angrily

explanation.surface: A censor ends a session by repeatedly finding fault with everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reverberating echoes and rings out loudly, which is what resounding describes.

clue.text: Angel in pain ignoring leader with difficulty

indicators.note: ignoring the leader means the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: an ache is a dull pain
a rub is a difficulty or snag, as in 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: A heavenly being suffers, struggling along in some discomfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' only links the definition to the wordplay; nothing goes inside anything. 'There's the rub' is Hamlet's phrase for a difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a winged child-like angel of Christian art, one of the orders of heavenly beings.

clue.text: Dancing in reel, had to be star attraction

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so they land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer had to top the bill by dancing a Scottish reel.
explanation.walkthrough: A reel is a lively Scottish folk dance, which makes 'Dancing' look literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The headliner is the performer billed at the top of a show, its main draw for audiences.

clue.text: Become less severe about period of fasting

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Someone softens their stance on going without food for a few weeks.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to give way and act more leniently after being harsh or determined.

clue.text: Call for attention suppressed by crook in past

indicators.note: something suppressed is held down and enclosed, so it ends up within the other word

blocks.note: yo is a shout to get someone's attention
a crook is a bend or hook, as in the crook of an arm

explanation.surface: A criminal's cry for help was silenced long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like a criminal but here means a bend: BE(YO)ND.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond and past both mean further than a given point, as in 'beyond the bridge'.

clue.text: Influenced element in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as the word is said, so its sound counts rather than its spelling

blocks.note: the metallic chemical element Pb, whose name is pronounced like the past tense of the verb to lead

explanation.surface: A chemical component was affected by what was said about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Led is the past tense of lead, and to lead someone is to guide or sway them, as influenced does.

clue.text: Development of valid idea by photographer

indicators.note: a development changes and reshapes something, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A photographer develops a sound concept, as one would develop film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the anagram. David Bailey is an English fashion and portrait photographer famous since the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: David Bailey is a celebrated British photographer, so he is an example of the defining word.

clue.text: Sort who yielded, not being inflexible

indicators.note: to sort things is to rearrange them, so the following letters are put in fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A paradox: the kind of person who gave way is described as unbending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' reads as a noun meaning type of person, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyed-in-the-wool describes someone with fixed, unchangeable views, like wool dyed before spinning so the colour never leaves.

clue.text: Show broker in trouble, not born to be tireless toiler

indicators.note: things in trouble are thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled
not here means leave out, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for born, used in biographies

explanation.surface: A theatrical agent facing difficulties is cast as a hard-working drudge.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove B from SHOW BROKER, then rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A workhorse is a person who does a great deal of hard work reliably, a tireless labourer.

clue.text: Brand new cloth

blocks.note: a line is a product range sold under a brand
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A label advertises a freshly launched fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brand new' reads as a single phrase meaning unused, but the two words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is a fabric woven from flax fibres, a classic cloth for sheets and clothing.

clue.text: Trendy religious community possessing name that is awkward

indicators.note: possessing means holding, so the word for the community holds the next pieces inside it

blocks.note: in means fashionable or trendy
a convent is a community of nuns
N is the abbreviation for name
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A fashionable order of nuns takes a name that proves embarrassing.
explanation.walkthrough: The convent holds two pieces, the name and the Latin abbreviation, placed after its fifth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inconvenient causes trouble or difficulty, making it awkward to deal with.

clue.text: Infamy in denial over strange rite in play

indicators.note: something strange is out of its normal state, so these letters are disordered
the jumbled word sits inside the word for play
in a down clue, over means placed above, so this piece is written first

blocks.note: no is a word of denial
to toy with something is to play with it
the letters of rite rearranged

explanation.surface: A disgraced figure denies that an odd ritual took place in a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the denial on top; the jumbled rite then goes inside the word for play, before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is fame for something bad, which is exactly what infamy means.

clue.text: Striking worker supported by a few

indicators.note: in a down clue, something supported by another stands on top of it, so that piece comes first

blocks.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
some means a few, an unspecified small number

explanation.surface: A worker on strike is backed by a handful of colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking worker' looks like an industrial dispute, but 'Striking' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome and striking both describe a person whose good looks are impressive and draw attention.

clue.text: Variety of clue, firm kind

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters appear in a changed order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter describes one type of clue as solid and generous.
explanation.definitionFit: A merciful person shows compassion and leniency, which means being kind to others.

clue.text: Dish, look, filled with wood and dark liquid

indicators.note: something filled with other things has them placed inside it

blocks.note: teak is a hard tropical wood
tar is a thick black liquid
to stare is to look fixedly

explanation.surface: A diner peers at a plate that seems to contain timber and black sludge.
explanation.walkthrough: The wood and the liquid both go inside the word for look, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak tartare is a dish of raw minced beef, usually served with a raw egg yolk.

clue.text: Boat operator in pub with expression of surprise

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
gee is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A sailor in a tavern lets out a gasp of astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' only links the definition to the wordplay; nothing is put inside anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargee is a person who works on or steers a barge, a flat-bottomed canal boat.

clue.text: Mix with number in endless activity

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter is cut
the first word sits within the trimmed word that follows

blocks.note: NO is the abbreviation for number
a hobby is a leisure activity

explanation.surface: Someone blends a figure into a never-ending pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix with' means socialise here, not combine ingredients.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to socialise or associate familiarly with people, especially those of higher status.

clue.text: Lover immersed in nostalgia mourned

indicators.note: something immersed is submerged within, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A wistful person grieves over a lost sweetheart from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a lover or love affair, often a secret one, taken from the French for love.

clue.text: One caught in deal worried by cold language

indicators.note: worried things are agitated and unsettled, so these letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A person trapped in an anxious business deal shivers in the chill while speaking a foreign tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal but its letters join the anagram, which is followed by C.
explanation.definitionFit: Icelandic is the North Germanic language spoken in Iceland, so it is an example of a language.

clue.text: Large test, not small

indicators.note: not here means without, so a letter is left out

blocks.note: to sample something is to try or test it
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A big examination, rather than a little one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful or generously sized, so it is a synonym for large.

clue.text: Doctor interrupted by anarchic ring, rogue faction

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing break into its middle, so the rest goes inside
anarchic means lawless and disordered, so these letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor in Britain
the letters of these two words rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor's work is disrupted by a lawless gang of villains splitting off.
explanation.walkthrough: G + INGERGROU + P. A ginger group is a British term for an active pressure group within a party or organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger group is a small, energetic section within a larger body pressing for change, a kind of faction.

clue.text: Bid without hesitation cancelled

indicators.note: without means lacking, so some letters are taken away

blocks.note: an offer is a bid
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An offer made without pausing has been called off.
explanation.definitionFit: When an event is off, it has been cancelled and will no longer take place.

clue.text: Beginning year, bishop reflected in musical style

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirror-wise, so the order runs backwards
the turned pieces sit inside the word for the musical style

blocks.note: YR is the abbreviation for year
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
emo is an emotional style of rock music

explanation.surface: A cleric starts the new year by contemplating an emotional style of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning' looks like a verb opening the sentence, but it is the definition, used as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is the earliest stage of an organism's growth, so figuratively anything in its beginning.

clue.text: Sad book with lines about end of fragile flower

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept
about means around, so the lines go around the kept letter

blocks.note: feeling blue means feeling sad
B is the abbreviation for book
L stands for line, so two lines make LL
the last letter of fragile

explanation.surface: A melancholy volume of verse is written about a delicate bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluebell is a woodland plant with blue bell-shaped blooms, an example of a flower.
